The only issue I had was the face recognition sign in, which seemed to only work about a fifth of the time. It's also a pity that the monitor wasn't 360 degrees too. However, overall I really liked the laptop. It was nice and light, and could fit in my purse really well. However, after 3 months, it just stopped working without any reason. There was no physical damage to the laptop whatsoever, I simply closed it like normal one night, and it wouldn't boot up 2 hours later. Monitor went black, and only the keyboard would light up. So while it was working, it worked great despite the iffy face recognition sign in. The touch screen was sensitive enough, and it woke up from sleep reasonably well timed. I've contacted Microsoft support and thankfully there is a 1 year warrante, however, it means they will simply just probably replace it with refurbished one. It's a bit saddening that it only lasted 3 months or so and that now anything on it will be wiped. Hopefully, the next laptop will be longer lasting. Overall, in working shape, it was relatively a 4 star. My only complaints were the face sign in, it wasn't 360 degrees bendable, and the magnetic charging chord often would fall out.

title: 3-Pound Chromebook with Nice Keyboard and Good Display
text: The HP Chromebook 14-inch laptop comes with a full 1080 resolution screen. It has a small, 32MB SSD for the system software. It comes preloaded with Google Chrome, Gmail, YouTube, and a Play Store. It takes about 16 seconds to boot. The touch screen uses seven (7) different touch gestures, and if you're not going to use a mouse, you'll at least need to learn several of these. The computer comes with a built-in USB-C port for charging, and with an adapter, connecting this to an external monitor. It has a micro-SD card reader built-in. It comes with dual B&O speakers (Bang and Olufson), and has a built-in camera. It boasts an 8.5-hour battery life and 4GB of RAM. This is my first Chromebook. Overall, it's a decent computer for its size. It's not super fast, but at this size/cost, I don't expect it to be. But for web browsing, photo viewing, and web-based apps such as the Google suite and Google Drive, it's fully and perfectly functional. I also like the soft touch keyboard. Overall, good value for the $. If you don't need to do anything processor-intensive (gaming, photo editing, video editing, etc.), then this little guy fits the bill. Recommended!

title: Could not obtain full-screen display on an external monitor. This function should be pretty basic, should it not?
text: I've been a devoted Windows user since the early 90s. In parallel, and in counterpoint, I've also cycled through countless Windows laptops over the years, including Compaq, HP and Dell, and often been disappointed with the longevity of the machines. I nevertheless retained my affinity for the Windows operating system---so much so that when I purchased a MacBook Pro last year, I partitioned the disk and continued operating under Windows 10. I therefore greeted news of the Surface Laptop this spring---with its sleek and unitary design, and integration with other Microsoft products---with great enthusiasm. At last, I thought, the hardware would rise to the level of the software. The Surface Laptop would be Microsoft's answer to Apple. Alas, upon buying the machine (indeed, the highest-end model), I found myself severely disappointed. First of all, it ran noisy and hot right out of the box. Second, I could not even obtain a full-screen display on a standard Samsung external monitor (a defect which could not be resolved through a lengthy call to Microsoft Tech Support). How could Microsoft overlook such a basic requirement? After several hours of struggling I put the machine back in the box and returned it for a full refund. From Microsoft, I expected much better.

title: Died in 18 months
text: Update: I've had this laptop for about a year and a half and it just bricked. I was in the middle of working on a document and with no warning it turned off and won't turn back on. It was not hot at the time. I took the back off and nothing is loose. It's possible it is the power cable, but I believe I would have noticed the battery going to zero so my next guess is that the board is dead. Naturally my warranty expired 4 months ago. In sum, I can no longer recommend this laptop. Prior to this computer I had an ASUS gaming laptop that was 3 times the price of this one. I was very happy with it, I've had it for 7 years and it's still able to run MMOs, albeit at low settings. I now have a desktop for gaming and didn't want to invest as much in another high-level gaming laptop, but needed a laptop for work and limited amounts of gaming/videos/etc. Now that I've been working from home for a few weeks (thank you, COVID-19), I've had a chance to spend a good amount of time on this computer. I have not yet tried gaming on it so I can't speak about that - I'll have to come back and update later. I have been working, though, and it's been great, especially for the price. I tend to work pretty RAM-heavily - lots of programs open, lots of browser tabs open - I haven't had any problems at all. I will probably add more RAM at some point anyway, but the amount it comes with is perfectly fine. When watching videos, the screen is nice and crisp with good refresh, but again, I haven't played any games. It seems to stay very cool, which is great as my old ASUS ran a little hot. It's practically silent, which is also nice because my old ASUS fans were a little loud. The keyboard is responsive. The keyboard glow is fun - my kids love it - and it helps me type in low light. The color on the keyboard changes colors and "breathes" - it's fine for me, but I wonder if there's a way to lock it on one color... if there is, I haven't found it yet. It can easily be turned off if it's annoying, though. I do have a few complaints - not big enough for me to subtract a star, but I'd like to mention them nonetheless. 1. The trackpad is left of center. I read other reviews that mentioned this before buying and it didn't sound like a big deal, but it actually is pretty annoying. I, like most people, I assume, use the trackpad with my right hand. Whenever I reach for the trackpad/mouse, it's not where I expect it to be and I end up right-clicking when I mean to left click. I also touch it sometimes with my left hand and end up zooming when I want to just move the mouse. Not a deal-breaker and the fix is obviously to use an external mouse, but I like to have the trackpad option for when I'm traveling with the computer. I'm not sure why they put it to the left of center, but if they had to put it one way or the other, I'd rather it be to the right of center. Notes for next time, ASUS. 2. There are not separate home and end keys. The key is home by default and end with the FN key. I use the home and end keys frequently and having to hit FN to use end is a little annoying. I get that a laptop has limited space, but I would rather have had home and end be primary functions on two of the keys above the numpad and other functions be FN+ functions (I hope this makes sense). Or maybe the plus sign next to the numpad could have been smaller to allow for one more key. There had to have been a way around it. 3. I don't know why, but my space bar has a tendency to double space. I'm a good typist and type on lots of keyboards - I've never had this problem before so I don't think it's something I'm doing, I think it's something to do with the space bar itself. Again, not a huge deal, but just a little gripe. So in summary/TL;DR - Great laptop for the price, a few little tweaks by ASUS would make it even better.

text: Just Buy it, you cant beat the price/build quality/performance. Screen is beautiful, full HD 120hz and very bright. Keyboard feels great to type and play on. Battery is great, but keep in mind you need to have it plugged in to game of course. The Ryzen CPU is fast although it gets warm(more on how to deal with that below). The GTX 1650 can play anything @1080p med/high settings over 60fps no problem Easy to upgrade ram/HDD's as well! I got this mainly to play Apex legends(which it does perfectly @1080p 60-90fps med settings all day no issues!) And to start using Blender for 3d modeling and animation, which it excels at NO ISSUES! My Recommendations: Add a second stick of ddr4 2666 Ram, either a 4gb o 8gb. That will allow it to run in duel channel mode and increase the CPU's and integrated GPU's performance by around 20% Buy a second 2.5 laptop hard drive, it has an open bay for it. You can get a 2tb seagate HDD on amazon for around $50 Make sure to go to your settings* and update windows fully, then go to Google and search "Amd Auto detect" and "Nvidia Auto Detect"" and make sure to update your GPU Drivers(you have two, one integrated and one dedicated) Download a program called "Ryzen Controller"(use google search). Once installed the ONLY thing you should do in here is set the "Temp limit cpu" to 80. This will help with thermals so much! Trust me. I see a lot of people on here giving bad reviews saying they are struggling during game-play, that issue is because the laptop will sometimes try to use the integrated gpu instead of the dedicated gpu. This is an EASY fix. Make sure your power settings are set on "High performance", and make sure you are plugged into power. If this doesn't fix the issue. You can go into the Nividia Control Panel>Manage 3d settings>Program settings, then choose your game and select "Use Nvidia High performance graphics"

title: Budget laptop without the budget feel or performance. Great 2 in 1 product.
text: ****UPDATE 4 - 7/19/21 - Mainboard died and cost to repair is above purchasing new. Unit was out of warranty, but I purchased with a chase VISA card which extended the warranty another year. After submitting some documentation they reimbursed for cost of new and I re-purchased the laptop. Maybe I'm a glutton for punishment, but I really like the laptop when it is working. Dropped another star for poor quality control or using cheap mainboard components. ***UPDATE 3 - 12/2/20 - Have had several issues recently and wanted to pass along how I resolved them. Issue #1 was trying to boot up the computer after 12 hours of sleep and being unable to get the computer to turn on at all. Didn't matter if it was plugged in or not. The battery was fully charged. I tried holding the power button. No go, laptop was dead. As a final attempt before sending it in for service, I pulled off the bottom cover of the laptop and disconnected the battery cable for several minutes. I plugged it back in, pressed the power button, and the laptop booted normally. Everything worked fine after that and I haven't had the issue since. Issue #2 was noticing the laptop was no longer charging when connected to the USB-C charger. Even the charging LED wouldn't come on. The fix was to shut down the computer completely, then hold the power button for 20-40 seconds. The charge light came on and the laptop started charging again. **UPDATE 2 - 7/2/20 - Resolved an audio stuttering issue by turning off Dolby Audio processing in the Dolby app.** *UPDATE - 6/10/20 - Dropping a star. Sent original back due to crashing issues when waking from sleep. Wifi also dropped occasionally and had trouble reconnecting after sleep. New unit seems to work fine. Also replaced wireless card with Intel AX200 (need torx T5 bit to remove bottom panel). Much faster and no dropped connections. Still really like the laptop (and Amazon's return policy).* Original Review: Overall usability – Everything about the laptop feels well-built and like it should cost hundreds more. Incredibly fast processor, especially given the 15W TDP. The AMD Ryzen 4000 series processors (7nm Zen 2) have really improved the thermals and efficiency to the same level as Intel (or better). Between the 6 core processor and the PCIe NVMe SSD the laptop flies. Nothing I’ve thrown at it has been able to slow it down or make it stutter. Benchmarks comparable to my HP desktop with i7-7700 (if in best performance mode while plugged in). Applications open instantly in most cases. Comes out of short-term sleep instantly. Nice webcam privacy cover. Fingerprint reader is best I’ve used in terms of accuracy and speed. Fans are quiet under normal loads and a low non-annoying whirring when the GPU/CPU is taxed. Exterior – Very light weight (but not cheap feeling) and nice sturdy build. Feels like it will hold up well. Keyboard back-light adjustable. Plenty of ports. Hinges also feel built to last. Touchscreen – Sensitive and good feel (though I prefer matte to glossy). Works well with included pen. Bloatware – Almost none (uninstalled Skype). Speakers – Above average for price range. Not especially tinny sounding like cheaper laptops. Don’t expect bass though. The included Dolby equalizer software can help improve the sound if you don’t mind experimenting. Side-mounted front-facing speakers are well placed. Screen – Brightness OK for indoor use, but I plan to run it at 90% brightness even on battery because anything less is too dim. Colors are bright. No noticeable back light bleed. Battery life – Above average for price range. Really quite impressive. Could easily last half to three-quarters of the stated 10 hours depending on the conditions (clearly not doing anything processor or graphics intensive for the duration, but web browsing, office work, or video viewing). Wireless/Bluetooth – Some occasional random disconnects and trouble connecting after sleep, likely due to Realtek wireless card. Average speeds on my 5GHz home network. Keyboard/Trackpad – High quality feel. You can tell when you’ve hit a key unlike cheaper laptops. Miss the numpad, but knew it didn’t have one before I ordered. Trackpad not over-sensitive or unresponsive. Good balance, but still prefer a mouse. Graphics/Gaming – Played Two-Point Hospital on Steam at 1080p very high graphics setting. Not very graphics intensive or an FPS, but the game is newer and frame-rate didn’t drop below 30 in game. Game load times are ridiculously fast. Downsides – Mediocre webcam. Soldered RAM (not a big deal w/16 GB, but if it goes bad it is a big problem). Screen may not be bright enough for outdoor use and the glossy coating leads to reflections/glare when viewing from an angle. Wireless card not great. Stories of poor tech support (though, admittedly I’ve never interacted with them). **Don’t forget to create your USB backup drive from the Lenovo website for crashes/re-installs. Or have the Windows 10 ISO handy on a USB drive and download the drivers/apps from the website.

title: Great laptop, but its the little things
text: So purchased this laptop as I sold the previous gen of this exact laptop (AMD 3500u). To my sister for her at home college classes. So I have some background using these series of Lenovo laptop. The over all build fit and finish is much better then the previous gen, its actually smaller, depth and with, yet only a HAIR bit thicker. The case is sturdy and the hinges are tight! So the display stays at the angle you desire. The plastic is a bit more 'plasticy' feeling then the previous gen. Which had the 'softer' feel to it. But this plastic cleans better, a quick wipe and all the smudges and such are gone! They keys are pretty much your normal laptop keys, so nothing to write home about there. The power.... the R5 3500u, that I had been using was a powerhouse already, but I honestly was not expecting THIS much of a improvement with the 4500u. Games such as WoW classic and LoL, near high settings at native 1080p res, a good soild 40-60fps with V-sync on. I have not tried any other heavy gaming apps, but some other programs such as SecondLife (yes i still use that), run pretty darn good for this integrated GPU. I think we are seeing the start of dedicated graphics cards in laptops on the way out, if AMD keeps this up. The 256gb NVME SSD is quite fast, not as fast as a Samsung EVO/PRO drives, but still around the 2000 Read / 1200 Write MBs area so its quite snappy. 16gb Dual channel DDR4 is a welcome over the 12gb of the previous gen. The screen.. well its a screen, its IPS, its a touch screen. The brightness of the screen is best suited for darker environments as other have stated. Its kinda of the weakest point of this laptop if your looking for something that can be used outside a lot. The included stylus is very nice and quite fun to play with even if your not into the graphic use side of it. I will recommend a plastic style screen protector, as the stylus tip kinda 'catches'' on the glass of the display and makes a bit harder to work with fine movements, a plastic protector eliminated this issue. Battery, the life of this battery is stunning. Full brightness, I was able to pull 4+ hours of streaming tv while away from the outlet. It comes with a USB-C charger, but it can still use the previous gen power-block as it has the normal style charging port. This was handy in my case as I had bought two other power bricks to keep at my summer and work locations, so no need to buy more USB-C chargers. Ports and Misc. USB-C, HDMI, 2 x USB 3.0 and SD slot. Pretty much run of the mill array of input/output for ports. I would like to see just a mini-SD slot instead of a full SD slot. Would make for adding extra space to the limited 256gb with out having to upgrade the entire drive. Nitpicks, I will say there is a few things that disappoint me from my previous one, its all minor things thankfully. 1. So far...the back-light on keyboard does NOT stay on all the time, only when using it. This CAN be fixed via software update, so hoping Lenovo reads this and fixes it. :) 2. No hot keys for turning the touch pad/touch screen, on/off. Kinda hand if you want to eliminate mouse movements when your typing etc 3. Speakers are NOT as loud as the previous gen, despite them being forward facing now. Overall you can NOT beat this laptop for the power and price you pay for it. If your looking for something that will last a few years for power wise and not in to heavy gaming, this should be in your consideration for purchase. I'm glad I still upgrade from the 3500u, even if I did not own it for a full year, the power is amazing!

I know this because I first bought a sata drive and it didn't work. I called the hard drive manufacture and Acer. Both of which were not a lot of help and did not know most of the questions I was asking. This is an Acer Aspire 5 . There is a lot of different models of this. For example, there is an intel and an AMD version. Please make sure you know what model you have. When you search for hard drives, make sure you put the entire model and not just Acer A151. The only way to add memory that I found to work is to replace the original NVMe PCIe that the computer comes with. In order to install this you will need to reinstall windows because this hard drive will replace the one that comes with the computer. Look up Youtube videos on how to do this. It is better to not download anything to the computer like microsoft office before doing this, because you might not be able to download it again without having to purchase the download again. I used the following hard driver: Crucial P2 500GB 3D NAND NVMe PCIe M.2 SSD - CT500P2SSD8 The RAM was easy to install Also make sure you buy at the lowest price. title: Microsoft Surface Laptop - almost upstages Mac
text: The real grabber is the 13.5-inch screen resolution of 2256 X 1504; it catches yur attenion and won't let go. Your eyes will be attracted to it as if there was a magnetic pull. Then we proceed to a possible deal-breaker, the operating system. Win10S (S for Student) has security upgrades, but sprouted warts; you are limited to software packages available from MicroSoft App store only. The corporate honchos believe this restriction will maintain security, and to an extent, they may be correct. You will discover that Chrome will not run, while MS Edge will. Thus, you must make adjustments to Win10S; it will not accomodate all your wishes. Upgrade to Win10 Pro is an option for an additional $50, although it is presently a free option. The Surface pen is a $99.99 extra-cost addition that was once included in earlier Surface versions. Strangely, Adobe apps can't run in Surface, so your creativity might be stunted by this restriction. Sound reproduction is excellent, a real surprise considering Surface's ultra-thin case. Audio is really enhanced when the Surface resides on a wooden table. Another plus is the striking cosmetics of Surface - gorgeous. The Alcantara fabric on the console is a matter of personal taste; it might enhance your experience; it certainly won't detract from it. Surface is ideal as a portable, take anywhere laptop with functionality of a tablet. Typical battery life is 8 hours. Wireless connectivity is automatic, hassle-free. You are limited to a single USB3.0 port, though, which you may appreciate if you travel light. Touchpad performance has really improved the past decade. Tracking is precise, and clicks are positivem and no more wandering cursors. Will Win10S become the academic operating system of choice? The answer is entirely dependent on cost. The Surface will set you back approximately $1200. I cannot imagine too many school districts backing programs forcing parents to pony-up that much for a laptop- tablet hybrid, especially with an operating system that cannot run many user apps. Students won't appreciate that encroachment on their liberties. Bottom line: Win10S has superior security features, but uers can download and run only MicroSoft App store distros. The Surface platform is a joy to admire and handle; you will likely take it everywhere. Its cosmetics, audio, and graphics resolution are stunners. I believe MicroSoft has almost upstaged the industry, including Apple, with new generation Surface.

title: Pen doesn't work with Windows 11
text: Updating my review and taking away a couple stars. I'll leave the original review below. I recently installed Windows 11 and everything works well EXCEPT for the pen. The included pen was one of the main reasons I purchased this laptop. I've tried uninstalling and reinstalling the drivers, and I have not been able to get the pen to work again. I'm now trying to find out if I can revert back to Windows 10 to be able to use my pen again. My Lenovo Flex 5 14" 2-in-1 laptop arrived yesterday, so I've only just begun using it, but I have a lot of good things to say about it already. The build quality is impressive, which I'm pleasantly surprised about. I was a little concerned about it being that it's all plastic, but it feels very premium. My last laptop was a Lenovo U430 touch, which had a metal case. But that one had some quality control issues as the top and bottom parts of the case didn't line up well and there were some sharp edges. Even though this one is plastic, it looks and feels much nicer than my older Lenovo. There is a little flex in the screen and in the lower part of the chassis, but the keyboard has very little flex and the hinges feel very sturdy. Another thing I was concerned about was the display. I've read/seen some reviews stating that the screen isn't bright enough and that the colors weren't great, but I think this display will get the job done for me. It will mostly be used in the office on my desk, so I may connect it to an external monitor for more "real estate," but the colors and brightness don't appear to be an issue for indoor use. Sitting in my well-lit office right now with all the windows open, the display is bright enough, although I do need to have it on max. I definitely wouldn't recommend this for regular outdoor use, but it should be fine for indoor use. The surface of the screen is a little "sticky" feeling when using touch input. My older Lenovo felt more "glassy" and my fingers glide on the screen more like they do on my smartphone. This isn't a huge deal to me as I don't plan to use touch input all the time. When I do, I'm mostly tapping. It's only the swiping and dragging actions that feel a little strange. Even though the laptop overall is very compact, thin, and light, it is a little unwieldly in tablet mode, so I don't see myself using it as a tablet for long periods of time. My iPad is still a much more pleasant experience for that. The Lenovo pen works well and it's great that it was included with the laptop. I can see that being very useful. It's not as nice as the Apple pencil, so I probably wouldn't use it much for writing or drawing, but it will be handy for marking up documents. The last thing I was concerned about was the wifi connection, which I have heard negative comments about. So far the wifi hasn't been a major problem, but I have noticed a few hiccups. I was streaming music from Google Play Music last night, and there were several times where the music stuttered. I'm not sure if that's an issue with the sound card driver or the wifi card. Hopefully it will be corrected with a driver or firmware update in the future. At any rate, it's a minor annoyance that I can live with. If it doesn't get fixed, I'll probably spend $20 and replace the Realtek wifi card with a superior Intel card, since that component is user replaceable (although it would probably void my 1 year warranty). The computer seems to be plenty powerful, thanks to the Ryzen 4500u, the solid state drive, and the 16gb of memory. The fan keeps the laptop comfortably cool, and it's not overly loud. I have a desktop with a Ryzen 5 1600 and I love it, so I intentionally sought out a laptop with the latest generation of mobile Ryzen processors. After comparing this Lenovo to available models from Acer, Dell, and HP, this seemed to have the best set of features for the price. This laptop should do everything I need it to do, and then some. I have not tested the built-in camera or microphone yet, but the speakers sound very nice. Not really much bass, but the sound is better than I expected it to be. The finger print reader is very nice and works as well as the finger print reader on my smartphone—very accurate and quick. This laptop checks all the right boxes for me, and I can tell it's going to be a pleasure to use. I agree with many of the reviews that I've seen/read. This laptop will be great for office work, students, and casual gamers. This is probably not the laptop to get for creative professionals or those who plan to work outside. They will need something with a brighter screen with more accurate colors. Overall, I'm a happy repeat customer with Lenovo and I'm very pleased with this laptop so far.

title: All it takes is a little problem to make a laptop a pain to use! Update - unusable touchpad
text: UPDATE [Feb 2 2020]: Asus serviced my laptop in response to the touchpad issue that persisted through online troubleshooting. The turnaround time was acceptable, and their communication through the process was very good. Unfortunately, the touchpad issue persists. I have now found several threads online about this issue, and it appears to be a design problem. My suspicion (shared by some online) is that it is caused by radio frequency interference. Apparently the touchpad is susceptible to interference and ASUS does not shield the touchpad as many other manufacturers do. The laptop still performs well and is fine in all other aspects. If you use an external pointing device as many do, you will like this laptop, but be aware that I have done everything I can do to get this fixed, and in the end the touchpad is not usable for me. Oh, where to start with this one!? So disappointed... but this isn't a bad laptop. I have used other gaming laptops in the past, and this one stacks up well, and has it quirks like they all do. The good things include the keyboard, lighting, screen, weight, cooling and overall feel. The bad things mainly concern the keyboard, cooling, and the touchpad. The indifferent thing is the performance. I am not going to benchmark this or describe the performance in this review. It has an AMD Ryzen 5 3550H CPU and GTX 1650 GPU. You can find out if those will play the games you want using the Internet. I am happy with the performance of this laptop, and I feel as thought I had reasonable expectations based on the hardware. The memory and storage have been sufficient. It is always good to have an SSD. I have used other laptops with HDDs and hybrid SSD/HDDs, and while the additional storage is kind of appealing, the speed of an SSD during both gaming and simple everyday use is preferable. The screen looks great, but I can't say that I notice the higher refresh rate - I don't think most of the games I've played are able to get much beyond 60fps on this laptop. This is a tough laptop (literally, the product line is called TUF). Have you ever dropped a playmobile toy? They are made of plastic, and they bend or come apart if you drop them, but the plastic never breaks. That's what this laptop feels like. It is very plastic, but built in a way that I would believe it would survive a fall. I feel comfortable carrying it around, would put it into a backpack and not worry about it very much. It is not touch by being solidly built and heavy, but by being light and sort of flexible in a plastic kind of way. I have not dropped it, though. While it is definitely an entry level laptop, it does have the same lighting system for the keyboard as more expensive ASUS laptops. The lighting is well done, the backlight is useful in the dark, and it looks cool. The only complaint I have is that the power button is visible from the front/top and has a single red LED that clashes with the keyboard lighting. There are two other white indicator LEDs on the front/top that don't seem to clash as badly. Maybe I should just set the keyboard to red all the time? The cooling is a mixed bag. If you have not used a gaming laptop, get ready for a noisy experience. No gaming laptop is silent when playing games. Like others I have used, this laptop is silent or very quiet when the fan is not running, and gets very loud under full load. I have noticed that this laptop seems to be at low-level load more frequently than others I have used. That means there is low-level fan noise more frequently. Also from time to time while doing things like simply browsing the Internet, the fans will kick in and get noisy. I suspect my complaints about this should be aimed at inefficient websites and Microsoft for background Windows tasks. The bad things are probably acceptable, except for one. The fan noise is acceptable, even with the occasional spikes under normal non-gaming use. The kyeboard is nice to type with, but is kind of squishy. I don't notice it while typing (or maybe I do and I like it?) but it is sort of odd to watch. I don't mean the keys are squishy (well, they are a little squishy) I mean the whole keyboard is squishy. While typing, the keyboard kind of bends inward. I don't think there is anything wrong, and I don't think it is going to break or anything but it is sort of strange to watch. Perhaps this is part of the intended construction. I would believe it is part of the chassis being flexible to absorb impacts. The speakers are anemic. They are very tinny - much worse than other laptops. The speakers fire sideways under the edges of the front of the laptop. There is actually pretty good stereo separation, but this effect is lost if you put anything near the edges. For example, it sounds unbalanced with the laptop at the edge of a table when one speaker's sound waves bounce off the surface of the table and the other one is over empty space. The problem is also there is you use an external mouse, unless you use it away from the speaker. Probably not a deal breaker for most as you will use headphones, but I sometimes like to watch a movie while traveling, and I would not enjoy that on this laptop with the built-in speakers. It didn't have to be like that, ASUS! OK, what's the bad thing? It is the touchpad. It lags something horrible and I have not been able to fix it. It is unusable. It mis-clicks, stops for seconds sometimes, and generally lags almost all the time.It is also plastic-y and rattles and clicks when being used. On the plus side, when it is not lagging too badly, the gestures and scrolling seem to work well. I have used an external mouse with this over bluetooth and a 2.4Ghz dongle, and there is no lag there at all. So it is just the touchpad. This may be fine with you - you might never use it without a mouse - or it might make this a bad laptop choice for you. UPDATE - I found a setting that makes the touchpad problem much less noticeable (but sadly, not completely gone). This laptop has two GPUs - one in the AMD Ryzen CPU, and the second "real" Nvidia GTX 1650 GPU. To use the Nvidia GPU fully, Nvidia software is installed. If you open the NVIDIA GeForce Experience app and go to settings (gear icon) the setting for In Game Overlay is turned on. Turning this off helps quite a lot with touchpad lag. It is unclear to me why only the touchpad would lag with this on and not a USB mouse, but it might have something to do with the "I2C HID" connection the touchpad uses; it is not USB and may share a bus with the GPU? However, the touchpad lags when the Nvidia GPU is not being used... ?!? Who knows, perhaps ASUS/Microsoft/AMD will fix this (the touchpad is an "Asus Precision Touchpad" with ASUS drivers on an "I2C HID device" with AMD drivers. I'm sure there are Microsoft drivers involved there somewhere too! I have updated everything already, but as of Fall 2019, the touchpad is unusable in my opinion.

title: Lots of trouble with this Microsoft Surface Pro
text: I wanted a laptop with 16gb of ram and an Intel i7 processor - this one was recommended and price was manageable. Yes, it is pretty, sleek and fast but after the first month I started having problems with it. The first time it crashed I was able to pinpoint the most likely cause as Windows updates. There were a few that failed, then laptop continually crashed, had to re-build my profile twice. It slowly went downhill from there. None of the drivers would update. I know my way around a laptop (spent my career supporting workstations and laptops) so I started with the simplest fix and worked my way up. Could not reset or restore. Fortunately I purchased a warranty and they put me in touch with a very knowledgeable person at Microsoft and we re-built from scratch to Windows 10 Pro (10.0.19042 build 19042). Everything has been fine for a while but now it randomly crashes with an error of "WHEA uncorrectable error" which fortunately doesn't harm my profile but is almost impossible to identify the cause. I've run tests on memory and the hard drive and they seem to be fine. Very annoying and unstable, and this is the laptop I have to use for the next few years? I'm ready to go back to my old. slow HP Elitebook. Not a happy camper.

title: Great Laptop
text: Great price, fast laptop, great screen quality. Very very happy with this purchase. Works perfectly for Microsoft products and web surfing. I don’t game so I’m not sure how it would be as a gaming computer.

title: Noisy Fan + Awful Webcam- 16GB Memory no help
text: This is the first Apple product that I have purchased that I don't like. I love my old Macbook Air from 2013. At the time, it was light and slick and fast. Fast forward 7 years and the MacBook Air is the cheap the version of the Macbook Pro. It's barely lighter, and it's almost as powerful, but it isn't. I missed the 14-day window, but I want to return this for 2 reasons: 1. Noisy fan - Sorry, but using the web only, no movies up right now, just 8 tabs, nothing else open, and the fan is blaring. Sure I am not on a hard surface right now, but I am inside, it's cool, and this should not be happening with an Apple computer in 2020. The 16 GB of Memory I ordered makes absolutely no difference here. Another thing. I have an old iMac from around 2012. Not sure why, but the webcam on that is way better. This is actually one of the grainiest webcams I have seen. Had this not been opened from the beautifully sealed Apple Box, I would think it was a knock-off. I got it from Apple, not Amazon. If you are in the market, I would get a Macbook Pro or another brand. I purchased this because I imagined a slick, fast, lightweight computing experience to last a very long time. I didn't expect an annoying fan, and a webcam that is unusable. Wish Apple would make the MacBook Air a much lighter, and much faster computing experience while cleaning up any fan issues. It's really awful to have fan issues in 2020. That shows negligence, and an engineering team that is trending downward. The Macbook Air has turned into a mass consumption low brow model. Don't get it.

title: Factory reset within 3 weeks!?
text: So, I've had this laptop for about 3 weeks and I lived it right from the start. It's fast, it turns into a tablet, it comes with a neat pen stylus, and so much more. Until today. For whatever reason things just started to go wrong, starting with the screen rotation. One of the best features is the 2 in 1 of the tablet. Auto rotate is a huge importance to functioning correctly. Then I realized the keyboard no longer disabled when in tablet mode. Thus is kind of a deal breaker since there is no way to use it in that mode if the keys keep interfering. There are other small things I've been noticing, but none of which would warrent a return. I am reformatting now, which I definitely shouldn't have to do before I've had the thing for even a month, and I will update if the issues have been resolved. If not, and thankfully I am within the return window, it will be going back. Update: So I purchased a second laptop and while all of the issues on the old one are gone, I have entirely new issues on the new device. I don't know why they can't get it right! The display on the new laptop is very washed out and not a crisp as the old one. The whites are slightly gray and just not as clear. I'll be returning the old one and hanging on to this one for a while since the features I most wanted are working on it. For now. Stay tuned for future updates grrrr.

title: Camera has very bad performances
text: It has been widely reported that the camera on the 2020 MacBook Air is low quality, but mine was definitely in the non-acceptable range. Picture was very grainy, unfocused, and low light level. I strongly suspect the glass in front of the video chip was damaged, perhaps for a contamination during assembly, but have now way of checking directly. Cleaning the outside had no effect. With heavy heart, I decided to return the unit, and buy an equivalent from the big-box store, where quality can (and will) be checked before purchasing. Update: refund for the item still pending, 14 working days after the returned item was delivered to Amazon. Worse than expected and worse than advertised (14 calendar days)

title: Reliable gaming laptop, but low battery life.
text: This computer performance wise is very good for the price. I am able to play Apex legends and Minecraft with little issue with the the fps. The computer may have problems with higher graphics settings on more intensive games, but I have not tested this myself. My main concern low battery life. Off the charger the battery only lasts for a few hours even when not gaming and on battery saver settings. I wouldn't recommend it for multi use as a business computer if you travel a lot. But, if you are looking to have a reliable gaming computer that you can bring to your friend's house that doesn't weigh 20 lbs I would recommend this computer.

title: *UPDATED* Base Model Review (i5 Processor, 4 GB of RAM, and 128 GB SSD)
text: EDIT 12/02/17 -- I have returned this item to purchase the next model up (i5 processor, 8 GB of RAM, and a 256 GB SSD). While the base model was fast and was fine with my normal tasks, I couldn't get over the 4GB of ram at this price range. I returned the laptop because I'm afraid that a few years down the road, this won't be enough memory to last. I purchased the next model up from microsoft's website as it was on sale. For an extra $200 I get the better, mid-tier, model and peace-of-mind with the 8GB of RAM and the bigger hard drive. I highly recommend that if you're going to spend this much money, save up a little more and get the mid-level surface laptop. Original Post - To preface, I bought this computer at my local best buy for $900, and it came with a microsoft Arc bluetooth mouse (it's awesome). I purchased the base model with an i5 processor, 4 gb of RAM, and a 128 gb SSD. I bought this laptop because the look of the computer really struck me. As for the internals, at $900 you could probably get a better laptop. The processor so far appears to be good, and the SSD is blazing fast. The only thing that concerns me, is the 4 GB of RAM. Only having chrome open, with two chrome tabs the memory is already at 50% usage in task manager. I didn't buy this laptop to be a work house and do crazy video editing or gaming, I bought this to do simple things like browse the internet. The screen is insanely clear, I compared this to my macbook pro retina early 2015 and I actually prefer this screen over my mac. The keyboard is nice to type on, and the audio/sound of the laptop is more than adequate. The laptop itself is very light and easy to move, it reminds me of a macbook air. I'd say that, if you are considering this laptop, do your research and know what you're getting into. It's an expensive computer, but it looks DAMN good. If you only plan to use this laptop to use chrome and do other basic tasks, I would recommend the base model. P.S. None of these computers have scalabilty. Meaning you can't purchase more RAM or a bigger hard drive and install it.

title: Buyer beware
text: I purchased the Lenovo flex 5 two weeks ago. Its amazing,but think I noticed it suffered from IPS backlit screen bleed. After calling Lenovo they told me this shouldn't happen, and told me to return it. I inquired about the dobly system, and eye bounced me around 6 times because each customer rep doesn't want to find out. The problem is they are sold out, and Amazon can only refund me, and not even put me on a reserve list. My main source of income is work on a computer. I brought up a very valid point on how Amazon allows price gouging a 600 CPU to 800-900+, and they wouldn't allowed to report it because it was a third party's, and they didn't have report procedure for it. .it appears like people buy them up and resell them due to the limited supply. You literally have to compete with the resellers has soon as they have stock, because it took me more than a week and a 2nd supply to purchase it. It's pretty disappointing Amazon openly allows gouging. They say they care about people but they don't. I'm canceling my prime membership, and Lenovo failed by not testing the CPU properly for black light bleed. Again I love the computer. I was in denial that the bleed is just natural, but the Lenovo rep told me it wasn't, and I was thinking what if got worse and my month is up. This is the best CPU you for this price range on the market, and even though they are refunding me I will be looking to repurchase it. If you inteded on purchasing it make sure you test it for screen bleed.

title: The hinge broke due to general use, the warranty wouldn’t cover it.
text: I have used this computer for six months, and this is my second Lenovo I own. I primarily use it for drawing and it does a fairly decent job as a drawing tablet BUT just like other Lenovo’s in the yoga series it has issues with the hinges. Just through regular use switching between tablet mode and laptop mode, the hinge of my computer cracked, my computer was still under warranty but this damage was not covered. As a computer I genuinely liked this Lenovo model up to this point, it was exactly what I wanted out of a computer, but I highly doubt I will be getting one again after this one ages out. My previous Lenovo yoga ended up with a similar issue after a few years of use (after 4 years the hinge broke through the front of the screen) so I looked to get another Lenovo when it was time to replace it as I had liked my old one a lot but it would cost just as much to replace as to repair. I’m extremely disappointed in how quickly this computer fell apart with no warranty coverage for the issue. The computer was not dropped or in any kind of accident, it merely was being used as it was designed when it broke.

text: I don't even know where to begin. The first night I received this laptop I desperately needed the scan-record feature for an assignment for work. It failed each time I tried.
